title: Spatial state alias in a published adaptive-treatment assay

claims.statement: Appold et al. report spatially tracked resistant-mutant confinement and escape under time-modulated treatment in a yeast assay, with resource-mediated spatial dynamics and a treatment-schedule boundary; tumor and biofilm transfer is described as a hypothesis.
claims.limitations: The reductionist yeast system does not validate the mechanism or a steering rule in cancer or biofilms.

claims.statement: At frame 145 (72.5 h), P2 and P3 have colony areas of 308770 and 322430 px2 and two-hour log-area rates of 0.002909 and 0.002623 per hour, while nearest tracked clone-front clearances are 76.3 and 549.0 um. Under the final article eligibility and escape rules, P2 has one later escape (clone 15, first breach at frame 150) and P3 has no eligible breach through frame 251.
claims.limitations: Post-hoc two-colony comparison; it does not estimate predictive accuracy, causal effects, or policy value. P3's zero events applies only to source-eligible tracks through the supplied horizon.

claims.statement: In the adaptive cohort, P2 clone 15 and P8 clone 18 reach the same measured breach distance (2.59 um) at different times relative to the preceding and next pulses. P2 contacts 4.5 h after the previous pulse ends and remains within 80 um through 125.5 h; P8 contacts 23 h after the previous pulse ends, one hour before the next pulse, and retreats beyond 80 um 7.5 h after contact. This supports a candidate hypothesis that post-contact fate depends on front-growth state and dosing latency.
claims.limitations: Only two post-frame-145 contact events are compared; P2/P8 differences may reflect clone or local-neighborhood state. The source article already studies reconfinement and treatment timing. No predictive or causal effect, novelty, or policy benefit is established.

claims.statement: Generic spatial competition, adaptive therapy, clone confinement, growth rebound as a confinement proxy, and schedule steering are prior art; no priority claim is made for those ideas.
claims.limitations: This bounded check does not prove global novelty or exhaust the cancer-evolution literature.

claims.statement: The Barber/Couce Figure 2B supplementary workbook has some ML ΔmutH percentages that reduce to 20/21 and 18/21 (or integer multiples), not integer multiples of 1/48, while Methods report 48 parallel populations outside regime L.
claims.limitations: Effective denominators or attrition are not resolved; this is not a data-error claim and is not evidence for the spatial finding.

claims.statement: No new mechanism, theorem, prospective diagnostic, treatment policy, cancer validation, or clinical recommendation is established by this work.
claims.limitations: A prospective held-out assay could change the status of the clearance-feature hypothesis.

claims.statement: A prospective assay can test whether local sensitive-front growth, clone clearance, and pulse-relative contact latency improve prediction of breach and retreat beyond the existing bulk-rebound state and full treatment history, then randomize pulse-restart latency at matched total exposure to test causality.
claims.limitations: Unperformed; action mapping, sample size, segmentation error, and attainable prediction gain remain unknown.

rejected_routes.route: Generic claim that spatial population structure changes resistance evolution or adaptive-therapy response
Generic growth-rebound feedback as a proxy for resistant-clone confinement
Generic same-primary-resistance phenotype paths imply different collateral responses
Cancer or patient policy inferred from the yeast assay

restart_gates: Independently replicate under the source assay and prospectively preregister the escape horizon and feature set.
Hold out independently executed plate/chamber runs; compare the bulk-rebound baseline with the same-history model plus clone clearance, clearance velocity, and local sensitive-front growth.
Charge imaging, fluorescence, segmentation, latency, missed observations, and prior-treatment history equally across feature-ablation baselines.
Only after predictive gain, test a preregistered geometry-informed policy against rebound feedback at matched cumulative treatment and population control.
If events or image quality are insufficient, preserve UNKNOWN; do not claim clinical or cross-system generality.
